scenarioStory.history: Mother reports the child woke up two nights ago with a harsh, barking cough and has had a low-grade fever and runny nose since. Tonight the cough worsened and he began making a high-pitched noise with every breath, even while sitting calmly in her lap. No choking event, no known foreign body exposure.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew finds a 3-year-old male seated upright in his mother's lap with audible inspiratory stridor at rest, a barking cough, and visible retractions. He is anxious but alert and clinging to his mother. → Nebulized epi and dexamethasone given: Crew administers nebulized epinephrine and dexamethasone while keeping the child calm and upright in his mother's lap, escalating supplemental oxygen and applying continuous monitoring. → Stridor improved, transport initiated: Following nebulized epinephrine and dexamethasone, the child's stridor and work of breathing improve substantially. Crew transports calmly without lights and sirens, keeping the child with his mother, and monitors for rebound stridor as the epinephrine effect wears off.

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew finds a 3-year-old male seated upright in his mother's lap with audible inspiratory stridor at rest, a barking cough, and visible retractions. He is anxious but alert and clinging to his mother.

scenarioEvents.name: Nebulized epi and dexamethasone given
scenarioEvents.description: Crew administers nebulized epinephrine and dexamethasone while keeping the child calm and upright in his mother's lap, escalating supplemental oxygen and applying continuous monitoring.
relatedChecklist: Nebulized epinephrine 5 mg (5 mL of 1 mg/mL solution); may repeat in 20 minutes
Dexamethasone 8.4 mg PO (14 kg × 0.6 mg/kg; max 16 mg)
Escalate supplemental oxygen (nasal cannula → face mask → non-rebreather) to target SpO2 94–98%
Apply continuous pulse oximetry and EtCO2 monitoring as adjuncts to respiratory assessment

scenarioEvents.name: Stridor improved, transport initiated
scenarioEvents.description: Following nebulized epinephrine and dexamethasone, the child's stridor and work of breathing improve substantially. Crew transports calmly without lights and sirens, keeping the child with his mother, and monitors for rebound stridor as the epinephrine effect wears off.
relatedChecklist: Transport calmly without lights and sirens; continue to hospital for post-epinephrine observation
Reassess for rebound stridor at rest before epinephrine effect wanes; repeat dose if it recurs

scenarioEvents.name: Nebulized epi delayed
scenarioEvents.description: Crew prioritizes IV access attempts over nebulized epinephrine, agitating the child with the stick attempts. Increased crying worsens airway dynamics, and the child begins showing early signs of impending respiratory failure.
relatedChecklist: Recognize impending respiratory failure (fatigue, pallor, decreasing stridor/retractions); give nebulized epinephrine immediately
